question: After fixing BROTLI_QUALITY_RANGE to (4,5,6,7,8) and re-executing DECOMPRESSED-VARYING-BROTLI with N=20 per state, does |B-DECOMPRESSED-VARYING-GZIP - B-DECOMPRESSED-VARYING-BROTLI| remain <0.1 for the full 5-level brotli range, and does the /introspect compressed variation become >1 for error bodies at larger sizes?
hypothesis: H1: Decompression-normalization preserves discrimination at 0.5 under full brotli quality variation {4,5,6,7,8} because brotli.decompress() is deterministic for fixed input+quality and different logical bodies decompress to different bytes regardless of quality level. H2: Algorithm-equivalence holds (|gzip_brotli_diff| < 0.1) across the full 5-level brotli range because decompression-normalization is algorithm-agnostic — it removes Content-Encoding and decompresses, so the decompressed body is identical across algorithms for the same logical body. H3: Compressed-byte-only hashing under full 5-level brotli variation degrades to <0.35 (replicating binary {4,8} result with broader quality spread).
falsifier: Decompression-normalization discrimination < 0.5 under full brotli quality variation {4,5,6,7,8} (H1 falsified), OR |B-DECOMPRESSED-VARYING-GZIP - B-DECOMPRESSED-VARYING-BROTLI| >= 0.1 (H2 falsified — algorithm-dependent normalization), OR compressed-varying brotli discrimination >= 0.35 on /userinfo (H3 falsified — quality variation does not degrade compressed hashing), OR within-state decompressed hash variation > 0 (decompression non-deterministic).
baselines: B-DECOMPRESSED-VARYING-GZIP: hash decompressed body with gzip quality randomly selected from {1,3,5,7,9} per request — PARENT reference (result.json /userinfo_DECOMPRESSED-VARYING-GZIP decompressed=0.5, /introspect 0.5), not re-executed
B-DECOMPRESSED-VARYING-BROTLI-FIXED: hash decompressed body with brotli quality randomly selected from {4,5,6,7,8} per request (FIXED range, N=20 per state) — THIS EXPERIMENT's primary measurement
B-COMPRESSED-VARYING-BROTLI-FIXED: compressed-byte-only hashing under brotli quality {4,5,6,7,8} — THIS EXPERIMENT's secondary measurement
B-STATUS-ONLY: status code discrimination (compression-immune, expected 0.5 on /userinfo, 0.0 on /introspect) — PARENT reference, not re-executed
B-RANDOM: random fingerprint (null, expected 0.0) — PARENT reference, not re-executed
positive_control: Within-state decompressed hash variation = 0 for all states under DECOMPRESSED-VARYING-BROTLI-FIXED (brotli.decompress is deterministic for fixed input+quality). This verifies the decompression pipeline is deterministic across the full quality range.
null_control: B-RANDOM ~ 0.0 at all conditions (no spurious structure from compression artifacts). PARENT reference, not re-executed.
measurement_validity: Same mock OAuth2 server and CDN proxy infrastructure as parent (ports 5000/5001)
Same 4 auth states: no_auth (401), valid_token (200), expired_token (401), invalid_token (401)
Error bodies identical across no_auth/expired/invalid, capping discrimination ceiling at 0.5
FIXED brotli quality variation: quality randomly selected from {4,5,6,7,8} per request (5 levels, not binary {4,8})
Same frozen seed=44 for reproducibility (per-condition seed derived from parent)
Decompression via brotli.decompress() after Content-Encoding 'br' removal
N=20 per state per endpoint (4 states x 20 reps x 2 endpoints = 160 requests for DECOMPRESSED-VARYING-BROTLI-FIXED)
Parent gzip conditions {1,3,5,7,9} reference data from EXP-RUNTIME-35058619700 (not re-executed)
Parent fixed brotli condition reference data from EXP-RUNTIME-35058619700 (not re-executed)
Python 3.12.14, gzip mtime=0 for any gzip operations
decision_rule: SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST if ALL of: (1) within-state decompressed hash variation = 0 for all states (positive control passes — decompression deterministic), (2) B-RANDOM ~ 0.0 (null control — PARENT reference, assumed passing), (3) DECOMPRESSED-VARYING-BROTLI-FIXED decompressed discrimination >= 0.5 on /userinfo (H1 survives), (4) |B-DECOMPRESSED-VARYING-GZIP - B-DECOMPRESSED-VARYING-BROTLI-FIXED| < 0.1 (H2 survives — algorithm-equivalence for full 5-level brotli). ALGORITHM-EQUIVALENT if (4) holds. ALGORITHM-DEPENDENT if (4) fails (|diff| >= 0.1). FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING if (3) fails (decompression-normalization fails under full brotli quality). MEASUREMENT_INVALID if pipeline errors or sample size insufficient.
product_consequence_positive: If algorithm-equivalence holds for full 5-level brotli {4,5,6,7,8}, the product recommendation broadens from 'decompression-normalization works for binary brotli {4,8}' to 'decompression-normalization is algorithm-agnostic across the full brotli quality spectrum'. This enables universal deployment behind CDNs that negotiate brotli at any quality level, without algorithm-specific code paths.
product_consequence_negative: If algorithm-equivalence fails for intermediate brotli levels (5,6,7), the claim ceiling is restricted to binary brotli extremes and SPIDER must implement per-algorithm or per-quality-level normalization paths, increasing deployment complexity behind real CDNs that use intermediate quality levels.
estimated_cost: Low: re-run only 1 condition (DECOMPRESSED-VARYING-BROTLI-FIXED) with N=20 per state = 160 requests on existing mock infrastructure. ~2 minutes wall time. No new infrastructure required.
expected_information_gain: High: directly resolves the BROTLI_QUALITY_RANGE audit finding from EXP-RUNTIME-35058619700. If algorithm-equivalence holds for full range, the claim broadens materially (binary -> full spectrum). If it fails at intermediate levels, the design space narrows. This is the smallest actionable step that can change the C-MEAS-VALID claim ceiling. After this, the inherited real-CDN question remains the critical blocker.
